title: One Judge, Two Orders: Codex becomes an honest ruler

ciFast.note: The local release gates pass; the exact pushed v0.16.15 commit still requires Fast verification on GitHub Actions.

ciDeep.note: No real adapter comparison, model generation, paid-reference run, or browser-device matrix is claimed by this evaluation-contract release.

deploy.note: GitHub Pages proof will be recorded after the v0.16.15 main merge deploys.

liveProvider.note: This release changes offline benchmark, policy, analyzer, and reporting code only; it makes no provider call and changes no hosted model or adapter.

manualHuman.note: The declared primary Scion preference lane is single-model-judge. Human review remains a separate optional evidence class and is not claimed here.

claims.summary: Controlled comparisons can explicitly preregister one provenance-bound model judge as primary for the declared scope without changing or impersonating the qualified-human lane.
Model-judge scores and preferences bind the exact judge model, revision, prompt, source, artifacts, and scorecard bytes, with scoring required before pairwise preference.
A model-judged trial counts once only after A/B and B/A passes agree after unblinding; missing and position-sensitive passes remain visible and block the primary claim.

Scion promotion binds five frozen domains to ten trials each, two reversed-order Codex passes per trial, fifty stable outcomes, one hundred passes, and the existing score, preference, burden, factual, export, runtime, and device gates.
The release makes the Codex ruler executable but promotes no model or adapter, changes no weights or hosted inference, and claims no paid-reference parity or device result.
